top_comments.author: @TimperialBroadcastingAgency
top_comments.text:
I must be the only person getting increasingly annoyed with this game's abuse of thee, thy, and thine and I'm not even an English major! XD

For those not in the know but would like to care: thee = 2nd person object (I walk to thee), thou = 2nd person subject (thou walkest to me), thy = 2nd person attributive possessive pronoun (thy dog is cute), thine = 2nd person predicate possessive pronoun (the cute dog is thine) OR 2nd person attributive possessive pronoun before a noun with a vowel (thine axolotl is slimy).

Not that any of that matters, but knowing it made actually made the text harder to understand.

top_comments.author: @kirant
top_comments.text:
If anybody is curious, Azdimension (the developer of this game) is apparently Azerbaijan’s first computer game company. The developers were extremely young when they started (if I’m doing my math from the article right, the founder was 20 at the time). 

I think these details bleed into the game we’re seeing quite a bit. The hub world was quite detailed for what is clearly a game on a budget and it felt like they were drawing from experience when they made it. The selection of Azerbaijan within and of itself, as was the selection of basing it in Zoroastrianism, were hints that the location were close to the developer’s hearts. 

While it may not be a perfect game, it really feels like the developers tried hard and it’s really appreciated in the end product. I kind of wish Josh and Anthony went for a full series on it years ago. It seems like an interesting look into game development around the world.
